image.subject: A slender 35-year-old Chinese man with sensitive thoughtful eyes, slightly disheveled dark hair, high cheekbones, wearing a plain buttoned cotton cadre jacket over a fraying white shirt, posture quiet and introspective, sitting motionless in a dimly lit wood-paneled room beside an unplayed grand piano under dusty sunlight, holding a blank notebook close to his chest in solemn silence.

storyboard.claim: Sparrow preserves internal silence as zero so true music can eventually re-emerge without compromise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sparrow sitting introspectively beside a grand piano, guarding a notebook to his chest in the quiet room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the theme of silence and internal immigration from beat 319.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the physical quietude and steadfast cost of internal preservation.

image.subject: A 22-year-old Chinese-Canadian woman with intelligent observant dark eyes, shoulder-length straight black hair, wearing an oversized knit wool sweater and denim, studying handwritten notebooks at a wooden desk in a modest domestic room in Vancouver, suddenly looking up toward rain streaking outside the window in startled apprehension.

storyboard.claim: Invites the modern viewer to imagine waking up to find their everyday cultural freedom inverted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marie looking up abruptly from her papers as rain lashes the window, realizing the fragility of freedom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from historical narrative to direct audience thought experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Brings the historical stakes directly into contemporary domestic reality.

image.subject: A modest domestic room in 1990s Vancouver, rain streaking outside the window, where vintage black-and-white family photographs and handwritten sheet music scores lie scattered across a dark wooden table beside a vintage metronome and a fountain pen.

storyboard.claim: Personal photographs, private music, and self-expression become suddenly criminalized contraband.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Family photographs and delicate sheet music scattered on a desk framed like forbidden contraband artifacts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands on the specific personal treasures threatened by state prohibition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the physical intimacy of family photographs and musical scores.

image.subject: A charismatic 30-year-old Chinese pianist with sharp intense eyes, neat swept-back black hair, lean athletic frame, wearing a crisp dark wool tunic or pressed shirt, carrying an aura of guarded vigilance, standing rigid under high iron loudspeakers mounted on stone columns in a formal courtyard, casting a tense downward glance under harsh political banners.

storyboard.claim: Totalitarian power demands individuals discard identity and perform state loyalty under threat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kai standing rigid beneath public loudspeakers in the conservatory courtyard, gripped by coercive demands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the brutal alternative of state compliance and coercion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls Kai's historical struggle between survival and self-betrayal.

storyboard.claim: Poses the closing question: what core truth or story would you memorize to preserve your soul?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kinetic typography question archetype prompting deep reflection on personal memory and resistance.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHAT IS YOUR BOOK OF RECORDS?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the entire book summary with an evocative open question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Focuses the viewer completely on the titular concept of The Book of Records without visual distraction.
